name: Croatia (Zagreb)
kernel_parts_used: Schedule (ZPD čl. 19 two local rates; kernel theorems ticks_mono_of_progressive, ticks_convex, ticks_lipschitz_of_progressive, ticks_le_maxRate_mul, splitting_le_separate instantiated; every rate pair allowed by čl. 19.a st. 2 proved progressive for all rates)
Allowance.Taper + Family.reducedBase (ZD čl. 21.a pension-base reduction; Taper.amount_step, amount_le_full)
Table (paušal classes, Pravilnik čl. 3) and Table.perPeriod (monthly contributions)
kernel_gaps: Young workers' relief: a credit equal to a share of the tax on the lower band, prorated by the share of wages in the dohodak (ZPD čl. 46 st. 2): local
Means-tested benefit with five all-or-nothing brackets on income per household member (doplatak za djecu čl. 16-18): local list lookup
Allowance split between parents as an internal cheapest-of election (ZPD čl. 17 st. 5); the harness elections file is not used
Monthly rules without annual equalisation (ZD čl. 21.a, 204): perPeriod covers even pay only; uneven pay needs an explicit month list (eeContribMonths)

Owner-manager company side for HR in harness company.json is the OECD placeholder (CIT 18 %, no 10 % small-company rate, no director's minimum base): statute-cited side in tools/owner_hr.py, sent to kernel INBOX

headline: Croatian 2025 model (Zagreb) in Lean, agreeing with Porezna uprava's own calculator on 4,176 of 4,176 cases; it finds three errors in the tax administration's worked examples for young workers, a wrong rate in its calculator, a statute gap on out-of-range city rates (Knin), and two new loopholes: one euro of income can cost a family 742 € of child benefit, and paying a year's wages unevenly across months escapes 781 € of pension contributions because the 2024 low-pay base reduction and the monthly cap are never settled over the year.
